title: Retrospective pre-movement left-choice probability from brain-wide spikes
scientific_question: Within separately calibrated sessions, does neural activity in the one second before the known movement onset improve left-choice probabilities beyond signed stimulus and lawful preceding-trial history, with block-prior context tested separately?
primary_outputs: Binary recorded choice: right=0 and left=1; candidate returns P(left). No-response trials and source-invalid trials retain explicit source dispositions.

recording_contract.labels: TS1 choice,wheel and other behavior via published readout specifications; trial_id,values,timestamps,mask; anatomy and QC metadata
recording_contract.time_alignment: Readout uses trailing fixed1second target; context up to20seconds backed by split gaps; target-specific timestamps and masks
recording_contract.biological_ids: Session UUID/eid, subject metadata; publisher reports disjoint126/13animals

primary.name: Animal-macro left-choice log loss
primary.aggregation: Pool required held trials across sessions within each animal, calculate mean log loss, then equal-weight all 13 animals; the historical single-session route reports its own 93-query mean.
primary.rationale: A proper probability score rewards calibrated known-choice inference; balanced accuracy alone loses confidence information.

secondary: Brier score, balanced accuracy at p_left>=0.5, tie-correct AUC and class/support counts.
Paired SH versus SHN and SBH versus SBHN neural gains; SH versus SBH privileged-context gains.
Per-session and pooled-trial diagnostics, leave-one-animal and leave-one-lab summaries.

nuisance_controls: Movement-onset alignment is an explicit retrospective privilege.

evaluation.uncertainty: Retain all 13 paired animal effects and seven-lab dependence. Source uses 1,999 deterministic animal resamples, explicitly an unqualified conditional spread without refitting or exchangeability assurance; no binary success/p-value claim follows.
evaluation.failure_policy: Require one finite [0,1] probability and exact session/case/ordinal/unit/config/state identity for every expected held trial. Missing or duplicate rows, failed commitments and invalid probabilities make the complete session/animal endpoint unavailable; supported subsets remain descriptive only. One-class BA/AUC is undefined, not zero.
